claim: public.house_till_lines (migration the_cellar_reads_the_tills_own_record, ADR 0301 §1) is the till's own record: every item of every pos_checks row that is not voided, UNION ALL the pos_unresolved_lines rows with no pos_checks row behind them on (restaurant_id, source, external_check_id), resolved or not, so a queued line whose check exists is counted once, from its check, and an orphan (the Toast direct path writes no check) is still counted. Neither half filters on `resolved`: no code sets it, and dropping a resolved orphan would lose a sale. house_till_lines and house_till_names are revoked from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated. The verify holds while, in the newest migration that defines public.house_till_lines (comments stripped), the function body splits on UNION ALL into a check half that reads public.pos_checks c with `AND NOT c.voided` and never says `resolved`, and a queue half that reads public.pos_unresolved_lines u, ends in NOT EXISTS over public.pos_checks c matching all three key columns, and never says `resolved`; and both functions carry that REVOKE. Behaviour (voided lines out, a queued line with its check counted once, an orphan and a resolved orphan counted) is pinned by that migration's SQL test under supabase/tests.
